critiques.notes: Bro, it lands on an-Nas — the surah literally everybody recites, so search intent is permanent and the 'whisperer = the star that vanishes at dawn' is a real screenshot line. My only worry is the payoff ('his move is retreat, not power') needs to hit in the first 90 seconds or it reads academic. Lives in the crowded Shaytan cluster but the khunnas/khannas link is genuinely untouched, so it earns its spot.

The 'verb that only ever stamps a heart' is airtight and checkable — Khalil and Yusuf will love it — but this is the third proposal in this same pool riding the tab'a heart-seal exhibit and it's a sibling to the already-shipped qalb-sealed-rusted. For my phone-first crowd there's no share unit here; it's a grammar-lesson piece. The sharaha-opens-chest half (16:106 opened TO disbelief) is the only fresh, warm hook — build around that.

'You don't shake the earthquake, you get shaken' is a strong permission line for Amina and needs zero Arabic — that's the gold. But welding zulzila to yuqa risks feeling like two articles stapled together, and 'passive voice as theology' takes a beat to click on a 6-inch screen. Nail the opening sentence and it works; bury the lede and the two-in-three tap away.

'One letter = threat vs gift' is a made-for-Instagram headline, no notes. Problem is the body carries two separate mechanics (preposition swap AND pronoun pivot) and asks a casual reader to hold both — that's a lot of load for the format. The gharra them-to-you turn (82:6 addressing YOU) is the self-implicating hook; I'd almost split it off as its own tighter piece.

This is the one. 'The command to recite slowly is God asking you to do what He already did' answers a question every single reciting Muslim has actually asked — that's return-visit fuel. And Luqman whispering the courtroom's smallest unit to his son is exactly Sara's WhatsApp forward. Two exhibits but one clean idea (verbatim repetition), so it doesn't feel stapled. High audience pull, ships this week.

'Light and fire are the same word' is a killer hook and it arms the recommender for a verse adversaries love (blowing out God's light). Just guard the register — the nur/nar closeness has to stay morphological, not 'ooh spooky sound,' or a sharp critic dismisses the whole thing. Distinguish clearly from the published ibrahim-fire-cool-peaceful. Solid apologetics-facing piece for Khalil and Yusuf.

'You are the collateral' is a genuinely arresting reframe and the accountability-vocab lane is wide open. But it's a heavy, somber piece — my under-25s don't screenshot dread at 11pm. Pair the ending with the redemption side or it just sits on the chest. Three verses only, so keep the 'the Quran always' instinct in check.

This is the single strongest permission piece in the whole pool for Amina, my largest segment — 'God's tenderest name shows up exactly where you brace for wrath' is instantly sayable, shareable, and it quietly kills the 'Quran only threatens' caricature. No Wadud article exists (the love pieces are all حبب). One flag: it's a dead ringer for YASMIN-2 — same reveal, pick one. I'd take whichever draft keeps the sin unsoftened.

This is the best-framed of the three tab'a-seal proposals because it's positioned squarely as the defense against 'the Quran predestines you to hell' — that's real Yusuf/Khalil demand. But it's overlapping ZAYNAB-2 and YASMIN-3 in-panel and siblings the shipped qalb-sealed-rusted. Theologically the hottest thing here; if it ships, Hasan reads the draft first, non-negotiable. Low pull for the sharers.

'The word for where the dead wait is a word for the sea' — that's a wonder-hook a 16-year-old actually stops scrolling for, and the two-seas-that-touch-but-never-blend image makes an abstract eschatology word concrete. Fresh lane. The trap is discipline: barzakh is buried in grave-punishment folklore, so this has to stay Quran-only and NOT overplay the science angle, or it drifts into the exact weak material we're supposed to replace.

'The first person to say a'udhu billah wasn't running from the devil — it was Musa, running from becoming a mocker' is a lovely fresh hook. But it's stacked in the high-traffic Shaytan cluster next to weapons-against-waswasa and footsteps, AND it reuses ZAYNAB-1's khunnas link — so between the two, the panel keeps one. Two welded threads need one payoff or it splits attention.

'Peace enters the Book as something you can turn away and leaves as something nothing can interrupt' — that last line IS the screenshot, done. And it takes 4:94, a combat-adjacent verse the adversaries quote, and turns it into a mercy reveal with the ruling visible — that's exactly Amina's and Sara's search path plus the honest-contested-verse work the site is best at. Just scope tight to the salam noun so the count doesn't collapse into the ubiquitous root. Top tier for my lens.

A single concrete object — the shirt — is the most shareable unit in this whole pool: teen-readable, WhatsApp-native, 'the cloth that carried the crime carried the cure' travels with zero Arabic. Yusuf traffic is already there and nothing touches the shirt. The comparative-Genesis angle is the right instinct for outsider readers — just give Joseph's coat dignity, no deficient-predecessor staging, and don't claim the healing detail is 'unique' without qualification.

Same reveal as HASAN-2 and just as strong for Amina — mercy-name dropped exactly where mercy seems impossible is the doorway for the reconnector segment. Yasmin's added value is the honest 'God is love' comparative frame for the mixed audience. It's a duplicate, so this and HASAN-2 can't both ship; I lean toward whichever keeps the register un-sentimental and the sin unsoftened.

Third variant of the tab'a heart-seal claim in this pool (see ZAYNAB-2, HASAN-3) plus sibling to the shipped qalb-sealed-rusted. Yasmin's framing as the answer to 'does God seal people against their will?' is the right contested-verse angle, but on audience it's the same grammar-piece problem — Khalil and Yusuf yes, no share unit for the sharers. Panel should collapse the three tab'a proposals into one.

I respect the falsifiable-absence-law ambition, and it's catnip for Yusuf and the recommenders. But two problems through my lens: the 'expected ~8 collisions' rests on an independent-distribution assumption that a sharp skeptic pokes in one line, and loosening to adjacent verses yields nine — that wobble undercuts the clean claim. And for Amina/Sara a probability argument is cold; nobody screenshots 'expected 8, found 0' at 11pm. Ship only if the method disclosure is bulletproof and you accept it's a niche, recommender-only piece.

The 'ask early vs ask too late' light arc is nice, but the published musa-fire-three-tellings-quran already owns the Musa-fire scene AND the 'borrow a flame' framing — so the only genuinely new payload is the third occurrence, the hypocrites and the wall at 57:13. That's thin to carry a whole article. If it runs it must be an explicit sequel built entirely on the wall, not a retelling of the night borrowing, or it reads as recycled.

A rare non-technical, no-Arabic-required reveal for the WhatsApp parent — 'laughing and crying enter together and leave on very different terms' is a clean image Sara can say out loud. The honesty hazard is real: the laughter that gets the last word is at the disbelievers' expense (83:34), so don't sell it as a warm feel-good arc — name the discomfort or a thoughtful reader feels the sleight of hand. State mushaf-order clearly. Good sharer-segment piece.
